critical_operation.description: The HTTP/1 server header loop handles every Transfer-Encoding header independently. A value that contains 'chunked' sets is_te_chunked and switches the decoder to CHUNKED, but a later Transfer-Encoding value that is not chunked neither clears that flag nor changes the decoder. The post-loop guard at line 261 only rejects the request when no Transfer-Encoding value was chunked, so 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' followed by 'Transfer-Encoding: afterlol' is accepted as a chunked body. RFC 7230 section 3.3.3 requires the final encoding to be chunked; an upstream proxy that follows the rule sees a different message boundary, enabling request smuggling. The fix adds an else branch that sets is_te_chunked = false, so any non-chunked value invalidates the request.

entry_point.description: Untrusted HTTP/1.1 request headers are parsed here; every Transfer-Encoding header value is examined in file order.

trace.description: Header loop visits each Transfer-Encoding value in order
